briefings.title: What History Tells Us About the AI Revolution | Tyler Cowen & Alex Imas
briefings.tldr: While AI capabilities are advancing at a hockey-stick pace, economists Tyler Cowen and Alex Imas argue that economic transformation and GDP growth will be far more gradual than Silicon Valley’s "fast takeoff" proponents expect, constrained by institutional inertia, falling token prices, and the fact that AI agents still struggle to coordinate at scale.

briefings.title: The better AI gets, the smaller its share of the economy might get – Alex Imas and Phil Trammell
briefings.tldr: The economic impact of AGI will be determined by whether AI behaves like electricity (distributing downstream benefits widely) or social media (concentrating rents), making the strategic indexing of global capital gains a more vital survival strategy for non-AI nations than localized job-retraining programs.
